title: The Khovanov to Floer spectral sequence

items.title: Double branched cover of an oriented link

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §§1–2
Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Theorem 1.38 and Proposition 1.39

items.axiom_use: Assumes AC through the link-complement manifold and covering-space hypotheses; the mod-two meridian character itself is choice-free.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r$ be a nonempty finite oriented smooth link in the standard oriented three-sphere, and put $X_L=S^3\setminus L$. A small meridian about $K_i$ is the boundary of a normal disk fiber; its orientation is immaterial modulo two. The mod-two meridian character is the homomorphism $\epsilon_L:\pi_1(X_L)\to\mathbb Z/2$ that sends every component meridian to $1$. For each $K_i$, choose an oriented tubular chart, meaning a diffeomorphism from a normal disk bundle onto a neighborhood, written $\varphi_i:(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)\times D^2\to N_i$ and respecting the core orientation. Let $\lambda_i$ be the parallel longitude given by $\varphi_i((\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)\times\{z_0\})$ for a fixed $z_0\in\partial D^2$, and set $\eta_i=\epsilon_L([\lambda_i])\in\{0,1\}$. The double branched cover $\Sigma(L)$ is the closed three-manifold obtained by taking the connected two-sheeted cover of $X_L$ classified by $\ker\epsilon_L$ and extending it over each $K_i$ with local normal-disk model $(s,z)\mapsto(s,e^{\mathrm i\eta_i s}z^2)$ in these coordinates. Give its total space the orientation for which the covering map is orientation-preserving away from the branch locus.

items.title: Filtered convergence and the scope of the Ozsváth–Szabó construction

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, Remark 1.1
Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Lipshitz, Heegaard Floer Homologies, §5

items.axiom_use: Choice-free; the filtration is finite and all arguments are degreewise.
items.statement: Let $(C,d,F)$ be a filtered chain complex over a field with an increasing filtration $0=F_{-1}C\subseteq F_0C\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_nC=C$ and $d(F_pC)\subseteq F_pC$. Its spectral sequence stabilizes and abuts to $H(C)$ with the image filtration, without any uniform bound outside the finite range $0\le p\le n$. If a particular filtered complex has been constructed from a fixed link diagram, this convergence assertion does not itself identify filtered complexes arising from different diagrams.

items.title: Existence and isotopy invariance of the double branched cover of a link

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §2, Proposition 2.1
Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, §3.3 and Theorem 1.38

items.axiom_use: Assumes AC only through the supplied link-complement and covering-classification hypotheses; the mod-two homology character is choice-free.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every nonempty finite oriented smooth link $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$, the homomorphism $\epsilon_L:\pi_1(S^3\setminus L)\to\mathbb Z/2$ sending every component meridian to $1$ is well-defined and surjective. Its connected cover extends over the link with a simple order-two branch model, independently of the tubular charts used to describe that model. If $L'$ is ambient isotopic to $L$, the resulting oriented branched covers $\Sigma(L')$ and $\Sigma(L)$ are orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic.

items.title: The double branched cover of the trivial two-arc tangle is a solid torus

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §2, proof of Proposition 2.1

items.axiom_use: Assumes AC only through the compact-surface classification and the link branch-cover interfaces.
items.statement: Let $B=D^2\times[0,1]$ be a three-ball and let $A=\{a_1,a_2\}\times[0,1]$ be the trivial pair of vertical properly embedded arcs, with $a_1\ne a_2$ in the interior of $D^2$. The connected two-fold cover of $B\setminus A$ whose meridians about both arcs have monodromy $1\in\mathbb Z/2$ extends across $A$ as a simple branched cover, and its total space is a solid torus.

items.title: Link-surgery filtered complex for a double branched cover

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §§2 and 4
Lipshitz, Heegaard Floer Homologies, §5

items.statement:
Let $D$ be a finite regular diagram of an oriented link $L$ with ordered crossing set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The resolution cube has vertices $I\in\{0,1\}^n$, and $D(I)$ is obtained by applying the indicated local smoothing at every crossing. The link-surgery filtered module associated to $D$ is the direct sum
$$
C_D=\bigoplus_{I\in\{0,1\}^n}\widehat{CF}(\Sigma(D(I));\mathbb F_2),
$$
with the summand for $I$ in increasing filtration degree $n-|I|$. Choose the subordinate Heegaard multi-diagram, compatible perturbation data and top-generator cycles for successive attaching-curve systems. The diagonal component of the candidate differential is the ordinary hat disk differential. For $I<J$ coordinatewise, sum over every ordered path $I=I_0<I_1<\cdots<I_r=J$ changing one coordinate at each step. Its summand counts the zero-dimensional holomorphic $(r+2)$-gon spaces with input at the $I$ vertex, the selected top-generator cycles between each pair of successive attaching systems, and output at the $J$ vertex. The count includes the allowed source conformal parameters and imposes zero basepoint multiplicity. These are the surgery polygon maps; the component is zero if $I\nleq J$. Thus changing several crossings is a sum over paths and polygon counts, not an arbitrary direct edge map. The increasing filtration is $F_pC_D=\bigoplus_{|I|\ge n-p}\widehat{CF}(\Sigma(D(I));\mathbb F_2)$, extended by zero below $0$ and by $C_D$ at and above $n$. Thus a component increasing $|I|$ lowers its filtration degree and preserves every $F_p$. The cube direction and the reduced Khovanov cochain degree remain separate indices. The polygon-count finiteness, square-zero, and total-homology identifications are justified by the surgery lemma, which labels its actual Ozsváth–Szabó construction and top-input/filling calculations as external inputs, separately from the retained local analytic theorem and finite filtration algebra.

The local smoothing labels are those of Ozsváth–Szabó Figure1: in the chart with northwest–southeast over-strand, 0 joins the two left and two right endpoints, and 1 joins the two top and two bottom endpoints. These become A and B on the mirror chart, respectively. This fixes the convention for the consumers without a diagram-invariance assertion. The general surgery lemma also applies to links in arbitrary closed oriented three-manifolds; this definition is only its branched-cover instance.

items.title: A two-strand half-twist lifts to an annular Dehn twist

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §2, Figure 2

items.statement: Let $\tau$ be the positive half-twist mapping class of a disk interchanging two marked branch points and fixed near the disk boundary. Choose its standard supported half-turn representative in coordinates compatible with the local branched square charts, and take its unique smooth lift to the connected two-fold branched cover which fixes the annular boundary pointwise. Its smooth isotopy class relative to that boundary is the positive Dehn twist about the core when the half-twist orientation agrees with the annular orientation, and is the inverse twist when the orientation is reversed. A positive half-twist here is the usual supported rotation through $+\pi$ in an oriented disk coordinate containing the two points, interpolated to the identity outside that coordinate disk; the assertion is independent of its cutoff representative.

items.title: The genus-one hat Floer complex of an order-three lens space has rank three

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §3
Ozsváth and Szabó, Holomorphic disks and topological invariants for closed three-manifolds, §§3–4
Lipshitz, Heegaard Floer Homologies, §§2–5

items.axiom_use: Uses the ACω disk-count and positivity package for the hat complex.
items.statement: Assume the ACω hat Floer disk-count theory for closed three-manifolds. For either orientation of $L(3,1)$, the standard genus-one pointed Heegaard diagram has three intersection generators and its $\widehat{CF}$ differential over $\mathbb F_2$ is zero. Consequently $\widehat{HF}(L(3,1);\mathbb F_2)$ has total rank three.

items.title: Ozsváth–Szabó link-surgery filtered complex and exact triangle

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §§2 and 4, Theorems 4.1 and 4.7
Lipshitz, Heegaard Floer Homologies, §5

items.axiom_use: Uses the ACω analytic branch of the supplied Heegaard Floer construction.
items.statement:
Assume the countable-choice Heegaard Floer analytic package. Let $Y$ be any closed oriented three-manifold and let $\mathbb L$ be an ordered framed $n$-component link in $Y$. On its $i$th exterior boundary torus let $\mu_i$ be the meridian and $\lambda_i$ the chosen framing longitude. Use the three filling slopes $\lambda_i$, $\mu_i+\lambda_i$ and $\mu_i$, labelled $0,1,\infty$, respectively; $\infty$ restores the original unfilled component. For $I\in\{0,1,\infty\}^n$ let $Y(I)$ be the simultaneous filling specified by $I$. Fix an admissible pointed Heegaard multi-diagram subordinate to these surgeries and the compatible perturbation and top-generator choices used by the polygon construction. The mod-two polygon maps on
$$C(\mathbb L)=\bigoplus_{I\in\{0,1\}^n}\widehat{CF}(Y(I);\mathbb F_2)$$
form a differential with components only from $I$ to $J\ge I$ coordinatewise. It preserves the increasing filtration
$$F_pC(\mathbb L)=\bigoplus_{|I|\ge n-p}\widehat{CF}(Y(I);\mathbb F_2),$$
extended by zero below zero and by the whole module at and above $n$. Its total homology is isomorphic to $\widehat{HF}(Y(\infty,\ldots,\infty);\mathbb F_2)=\widehat{HF}(Y;\mathbb F_2)$. For $n=1$, the total complex is the mapping cone of the $0$-to-$1$ surgery map and is quasi-isomorphic to the hat complex of the third, $\infty$ filling; this yields the long exact surgery sequence for every surgery triad, with its cyclic ordering. For $n=0$ the cube is the single hat complex of $Y$. No filtered quasi-isomorphism between distinct surgery presentations is included.

items.title: Unlink resolution covers and the Heegaard Floer TQFT

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, Propositions 6.1 and 6.2
Lipshitz, Heegaard Floer Homologies, §5

items.axiom_use: Uses the ACω analytic branch of Heegaard Floer theory; the unlink topology computation itself is choice-free.
items.statement: For the $k$-component planar unlink $U_k$, its double branched cover is $\#^{\,k-1}(S^2\times S^1)$, with $\Sigma(U_1)=S^3$. Over $\mathbb F_2$, the hat Floer group of this cover is identified with the exterior algebra on a $(k-1)$-dimensional vector space, hence has rank $2^{k-1}$. Under these identifications, the cobordism maps for the saddle cobordisms between unlink resolutions are the multiplication and comultiplication maps of the two-dimensional Frobenius algebra $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$ after reduction at a marked component. The identification includes the marked-circle cases and fixes the basis conventions needed to compare the first surgery differential with the reduced Khovanov cube.

items.title: The trefoil double branched cover is a lens space of order three

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §3

items.axiom_use: Uses AC only through the branched-cover and lens-space convention suppliers.
items.statement: Let $T$ be either oriented trefoil in $S^3$. Its double branched cover $\Sigma(T)$ is diffeomorphic, up to orientation reversal, to the lens space $L(3,1)$ in the convention in which $L(p,q)$ is the $p/q$ filling of the standard unknot exterior. In particular, $\pi_1(\Sigma(T))$ is cyclic of order three.

items.title: Reduced Khovanov cohomology of a based link over F2

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §5
Shumakovitch, Torsion of the Khovanov homology, §2.2
Turner, A hitchhiker’s guide to Khovanov homology, §1.2

items.statement: Let $(D,p)$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram with a marked point $p$ away from crossings, and let $C(D;\mathbb F_2)$ be its normalized Khovanov cochain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the algebra $\mathcal A=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$ with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$. On each resolution state, let $X_p$ multiply by $X$ on the circle containing $p$ and act as the identity on the other circle factors. Define the reduced complex by $\widetilde C(D,p)=C(D;\mathbb F_2)/\operatorname{im}X_p$, with the surviving based-circle label $1$ assigned reduced quantum degree $0$ by the shift $\widetilde j=j-1$. Its cohomology is $\widetilde{Kh}^{i,\widetilde j}(D,p;\mathbb F_2)$. The basepoint may lie on any component; for a link, independence of the chosen component is a separate theorem.

items.title: The first surgery differential is the reduced Khovanov TQFT differential

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §6, Propositions 6.1–6.2
Lipshitz, Heegaard Floer Homologies, §5.3

items.statement: Fix a link projection and its surgery multi-diagram. Identify each first-page vertex group with the reduced state space of the corresponding crossingless resolution. For every cube edge, the induced first differential is the mod-two map assigned by the saddle: multiplication when two resolution circles merge and comultiplication when one resolution circle splits, with the marked-circle quotient at the basepoint. Under these identifications the direct sum of edge maps is the reduced Khovanov differential of the mirror diagram in the Ozsváth–Szabó smoothing convention.

items.title: Reduced Khovanov homology over F2 is independent of the chosen link component

references.title: Shumakovitch, Torsion of the Khovanov homology, §§3.1–3.2
Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §5
Turner, A hitchhiker’s guide to Khovanov homology, §1.2

items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the proof uses only the finite cube, basis calculations over F2, and finite-dimensional linear algebra.
items.statement: Let $D$ be a finite regular diagram of an oriented link and let $p,q$ be any two points of $D$ away from crossings, possibly on different link components. Over $\mathbb F_2$, the reduced Khovanov cohomology groups defined using $p$ and $q$ are isomorphic as bigraded vector spaces. The isomorphism need not be canonical; no diagram-change invariance is asserted here.

items.title: The reduced Khovanov homology of a trefoil has rank three

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §6
Shumakovitch, Torsion of the Khovanov homology, §2.2

items.axiom_use: Choice-free finite enumeration and linear algebra over F2.
items.statement: Let $D$ be the oriented closure of the two-strand braid $\sigma_1^3$, with both strands directed downward and the positive generator drawn with its southwest-to-northeast strand over its northwest-to-southeast strand. Mark a point away from the three crossings, use the A-smoothing (zero-resolution) as the through pairing, and use the B-smoothing (one-resolution) as the cap-cup pairing. The normalized reduced Khovanov cohomology of $D$ over $\mathbb F_2$ has total rank $3$. The normalized cohomological and quantum grading shifts do not change this total rank.

items.title: The E1 differential of the link-surgery complex is reduced Khovanov

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, Theorem 6.3 and proof
Lipshitz, Heegaard Floer Homologies, §5.3

items.statement: For a fixed finite regular link diagram $D$ with $n$ crossings and a basepoint away from crossings, the first page of its branched-cover link-surgery spectral sequence, together with its first differential, is isomorphic as a cochain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ to the reduced Khovanov cochain complex of the mirror diagram $\overline D$ in the specified normalized grading shifts. The resulting second page is therefore the based reduced Khovanov cohomology of $\overline D$. The isomorphism is for this fixed diagram and makes no claim about filtered chain complexes for different diagrams.

items.title: Reduced Khovanov homology over F2 is an oriented link invariant

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, §5
Shumakovitch, Torsion of the Khovanov homology, §§2.2 and 3
Turner, A hitchhiker’s guide to Khovanov homology, §1.2

items.axiom_use: Assumes ACω for finite Reidemeister-move generation. The reduced-cube algebra and component-independence argument are choice-free.
items.statement: Assume ACω. For every nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, the bigraded $\mathbb F_2$ vector spaces $\widetilde{Kh}^{i,j}(L;\mathbb F_2)$ obtained by reducing the normalized Khovanov complex at a point on any chosen component are independent, up to noncanonical bigraded isomorphism, of the diagram and the chosen component. No filtered structure from a Floer construction is part of this invariance statement.

items.title: The Ozsváth–Szabó spectral sequence for a fixed link diagram

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, Theorem 6.3 and proof
Lipshitz, Heegaard Floer Homologies, §5.3

items.axiom_use: Assumes AC for the branched-cover construction and ACω for the Floer analytic package; this fixed-diagram argument does not use Khovanov diagram invariance.
items.statement: Assume AC and the ACω Heegaard Floer analytic package. Let $D$ be any finite regular diagram of a nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, with a marked point away from crossings. There is a spectral sequence over $\mathbb F_2$ associated to the link-surgery filtered complex for this fixed diagram whose $E_2$ page is isomorphic, with the normalized grading shifts of the chosen smoothing convention, to $\widetilde{Kh}(\overline L,p;\mathbb F_2)$ computed from the mirror diagram, and whose abutment is $\widehat{HF}(\Sigma(L);\mathbb F_2)$ with its image filtration. This is a fixed-diagram construction; it does not assert a diagram-independent filtered quasi-isomorphism type.

items.title: The Khovanov to branched-cover Heegaard Floer spectral sequence

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.2, and §6
Lipshitz, Heegaard Floer Homologies, §5.3

items.axiom_use: Assumes AC for the branched-cover construction and ACω for Reidemeister invariance and the Floer analytic package; these are distinct uses.
items.statement: Assume AC and ACω. For every nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, there is a spectral sequence over $\mathbb F_2$ whose $E_2$ page is the reduced Khovanov cohomology $\widetilde{Kh}^{*,*}(\overline L;\mathbb F_2)$ of the mirror link and whose abutment is $\widehat{HF}(\Sigma(L);\mathbb F_2)$ with its image filtration. The page identification is an isomorphism of bigraded vector spaces; this statement does not claim a diagram-independent filtered quasi-isomorphism type for the chain-level spectral sequence.

title: The Khovanov to Floer spectral sequence — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The endpoints do not determine intermediate pages

references.title: Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 5
Sharifi, Homological Algebra, §4

items.axiom_use: Choice-free finite-dimensional linear algebra over F2.
items.statement: The false claim is that specifying the isomorphism class of the total homology of a bounded filtered chain complex determines the isomorphism class of its early spectral-sequence pages. More strongly, the false claim is that two filtered complexes with isomorphic total homology must have isomorphic $E_1$ pages.
